# The canvas

The canvas is the board beside the edit where the person lays out notes, files and nodes that make a picture, a clip or
a sound, wired into each other. Nothing on it is in the film until it is put on the timeline. A node the person points
at (`canvas node `ID``) is there. A project can have several canvases; your steps go to the one the person has open.

`openfilm canvas` prints the board; `openfilm canvas apply '<steps>'` adds, changes, wires and removes nodes, all at
once, and the person sees it at once. Its `--help` lists the steps.

## Laying out what the person asks for

- **A storyboard or shots**: one row per shot, left to right: a note (what happens, in the person's words), a picture
  node wired from it, a video node wired from the picture with `opts.mode: "first"`, and every video wired into one
  `cut` in order: the cut's "Put on the timeline" sends the clips in that order. Keep each shot in a group named after
  it (`around`) when there are many.
- **A character who looks the same in every shot**: a note of who they are, a picture node with `preset: "portrait"`
  wired from it, then `fullBody`, `expressions` and `turnaround16` picture nodes each wired from the note and the
  portrait, in a group named after them. Wire the portrait into every shot's picture and video (`opts.mode: "refs"`
  or as a reference) so they stay the same person.
- **A voice-over**: a `tts` node whose prompt is the line to speak, with `opts.voice` a voiceId from
  `openfilm get voice` that suits the speaker (none: the service's first voice in the person's language).
- **Words for a node**: write the prompt in English unless the person writes otherwise; describe what is seen, the
  light and the camera, not the story's meaning.

Lay things out and leave the making to the person (they press Make, or a group's Make all) unless they ask you to make
them: then make each with `openfilm get` and add it as the node's version. Say what you laid out and what to press.

# Media

`openfilm get`: media for the film. First OpenFilm's own library, free, offline and CC0: `get music-search`, `get sfx-search`, `get transition`, `get effect`, `get filter`, `get sticker`, `get text` and `get template`, each `--prompt "<what>"` in any words and language; each match says what of your prompt it has and lacks, and `--take <id>` copies the one you choose into the project and prints what to put in film.html. Look there before writing a transition, an effect, a text or a template yourself. The rest is made by a service the person connected in Studio (Settings → Services): voice-over, music and sound effects to your prompt and length (`get music`, `get sfx`, at a cost), transcripts, images, image search, video and web search. Make music or a sound when the person asks for something original, when it must fit the picture exactly, or when the matches lack what was asked; when the person says which they want, do that. `get` alone lists what works now; for a kind not connected, tell the person which services make it and where they connect one. A video clip costs a lot: the person confirms it in Studio first. Its `--help` lists the verbs and their options.

Media can come from `get` (OpenFilm's library, or a service that makes it), any service the person uses (with its API docs and their key), or your own code. Save it under `assets/`.

When the person wants a service that is not built in to make pictures, clips or sounds (on the canvas too), add it as a provider: `openfilm get` ends by naming its folder, the contract it follows and a built-in one to read. Write it from the service's API docs, then try it with `get <verb> --via <id>` once the person has added its key in Settings → Services.

# OpenFilm

Run `npx -y openfilm@latest` and follow the manual it prints: a page that names OpenFilm's own skills, how a film is
made, its media and its canvas. Read the one a task needs before you start it, and run the manual again whenever you
need it.
